surprise: probe: label-use lookup took 52 µs at 1K turns and 437–478 µs at 1M (9×); a per-lookup sum over every use breaks TP-T16
resolution: compute ink in time independent of a label's use count (recent uses exact, older folded into an aggregate as in Petrov 2006); rank checked against the naive reference
clause: ink is computed in time independent of a label's use count; ranking equals the differential reference's outside the deadband

surprise: probe: Parakeet transcribes numbers as digits ('340') while owners often type them as words ('three forty')
resolution: number words and digits are one symbol for matching; rendered text unchanged
clause: a number in words and the same number in digits are one symbol for matching; what is rendered stays as written

surprise: probe: Playwright MCP 0.0.86 exposes 25 tools with 21.8 KB of definitions
resolution: keep browser tool definitions inside the browser sub-agent; the main band carries one line for browse
clause: browser tool definitions live only in the browser sub-agent's context

surprise: probe: Playwright MCP snapshot text differed by a few bytes between identical runs
resolution: compare snapshots by content in tests; never byte for byte
clause: browser tests compare snapshot content, not bytes

surprise: probe: the sherpa-onnx 2.0.3 pip wheel's Piper voices fail with no espeak frontend
resolution: generate synthetic speech fixtures with espeak-ng at test time (two distinct voices)
clause: synthetic speech fixtures are generated with espeak-ng at test time

surprise: probe: Playwright MCP 0.0.86 negotiates protocol 2025-11-25, not 2026-07-28
resolution: the MCP client accepts 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 servers
clause: the MCP client accepts servers negotiating 2025-11-25 as well as 2026-07-28

surprise: Omi firmware (main, Nov 2026) reports codec 21 (opusFS320: 320 samples = 20 ms per frame, OPUS_APPLICATION_RESTRICTED_LOWDELAY so CELT-only, 32 kbps VBR), not the 20 the constitution's src.omi names
resolution: the codec id the device reports selects the frame size (21 → 320, 20 → 160 samples) and libopus decodes both; CELT-only rules out a SILK-only pure-Go decoder
clause: frame size follows the reported codec id (21 → 320 samples, 20 → 160); both decode with libopus

surprise: Omi's offline storage is now a ring/custody record format (firmware transport.c storage records; app wals/sdcard_wal_sync.dart), not a flat file of frames
resolution: the app's port of Omi's storage sync reads the frames out; it uploads them length-prefixed (u16 LE + frame) and the server acknowledges the sha256 of that body once durable
clause: an offline upload is u16-length-prefixed Opus frames; its acknowledgement is the sha256 of the body, sent only after the body is durable

surprise: Anthropic's preserved thinking (Opus 5.5, accounts created after 2026-08-31) rejects a replayed thinking block whose prefix changed; removing all thinking blocks is allowed
resolution: TP's rules already fit: within an exchange the request only grows and thinking passes back unchanged; when it closes all thinking leaves together
clause: within an exchange each request extends the previous one byte for byte; thinking blocks leave only all together, when the exchange closes

surprise: the sherpa-onnx Go binding links its shared libraries with an rpath into the build machine's module cache, and a cgo build on Ubuntu 24.04 needs glibc newer than Debian 12's
resolution: the release ships bin/ and lib/ with rpath $ORIGIN/../lib, built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35)
clause: the release binary loads its speech libraries from $ORIGIN/../lib and is built against glibc 2.35

surprise: with even edit costs, a real word one edit from an often-used known word is cheaper as label + change than fresh at its English frequency (card 13.15 bits fresh; cart pointer + one 9.08-bit edit below it)
resolution: a word the English list holds is never recorded as another word (endings excepted); MDL decides only for words outside the list, with no more edits than the word's fresh cost covers
clause: a word in the ordinary-English list is never a near-match of a different word; for any other word, label + change wins only when shorter in bits than the word fresh

surprise: Petrov's single aggregate (latest use exact, the rest as one evenly spread mass with mean d) misranked irregular histories by 8% (past the 5% deadband), and one mean d inside a^−d underestimates by Jensen's inequality
resolution: uses fold into time buckets that merge only while width ≤ (deadband / d) × age and (spread of d) × ln(age) ≤ deadband, each integrated with the Euler–Maclaurin end terms; buckets grow with the logarithm of a label's uses (237 at 10K, ~414 at 1M)
clause: ink is a sum over deadband-bounded buckets, never over every use; its ranking equals the exact sum's outside the deadband

surprise: weighting τ by the store's own word information let repetition move trust: every repeat shifts the frequencies the weights come from
resolution: τ weights each word by its ordinary-English information, which no write changes; records are read from the innermost symbol around a word that has one, since labels formed later carry none
clause: τ moves only when an outcome is charged; its word weights are fixed (English information)

surprise: the opening fold was checked on the request without the spotlight it would carry: an opening request reached 16295 tokens against B = 16000
resolution: the fold check counts the request with its spotlight, and the spotlight is recomputed after a fold
clause: the request that opens an exchange is counted with its spotlight before the fold decision, and never exceeds B

surprise: the store serializes on one connection; a query issued while a cursor was still open waited on itself (assembler ranking deadlocked)
resolution: every cursor is read whole and closed before anything else queries
clause: no query runs while a cursor on the store is open
